name: cauce
description: One core for Claude Code: routes each task to the right model, effort and capabilities, escalates on evidence, and remembers what failed across repositories.

livespec.title: livespec code index
livespec.description: Use livespec throughout the flow: index the repository, route on what the index shows, brief every worker with a code map, give workers livespec's tools, and report what a change touched. On by default; runs the pinned release through uvx when livespec is not installed.

parallel.title: Haiku decides what runs in parallel
parallel.description: A task queued behind running work starts beside it when Haiku finds it independent of everything running and queued ahead; otherwise it waits its turn. Off: one task at a time per repository.

autowork.title: Start queued work at once
autowork.description: A task queued with ++ starts the repository's dispatcher right away, so it runs in a worker without anyone typing cauce work. Off: queued work waits for cauce work.

names.title: Haiku names sessions
names.description: Haiku names each session of an enrolled project after what it has been asked, in .cauce/sessions.json. A name you edit there is kept.

notes.title: Project notes
notes.description: Each project keeps notes of what it knows, by topic (business, code, decisions, conventions, environment), linked to each other and to the code they are about. Workers that pass add what they learned and sessions add what they established every few turns and before compacting (Haiku files them); workers get the relevant notes in their brief, and sessions read them with cauce recall.

scribe.title: The scribe keeps each session's thread
scribe.description: At the end of every turn cauce reads what the session's transcript gained, without a model and without touching the session: your requests verbatim, the files it wrote, the calls that failed and what passed after. Work the session sends gets the part of that thread it needs in its brief, the project's notes are filed every few turns instead of only at a compaction, and /cauce:relay hands the thread to a fresh session. Off: workers get only the task's text.

wake.title: Wake the session when queued work ends
wake.description: With Claude Code's mods: when a task this session queued ends while the session is idle, cauce starts a turn with its notice, so the session tells you and continues without waiting for your next message. Off: the notice waits for the end of a turn or your next message.

prune.title: Delete merged branches
prune.description: A branch cauce kept for a task (cauce/task-N) is deleted once its work landed: merged into another branch, squash-merged (HEAD holds every file it changed), or holding only tool artifacts. Never one checked out or one a stopped task may resume from; its tip stays on the task's events. Off: branches stay until you delete them.

plugins.title: Hand workers the neighbours you installed
plugins.description: Workers get the MCP servers of layout-inspector and rastro when you have them installed as Claude Code plugins (or on PATH), each with its own skill: layout-inspector for UI work, rastro for tests, run behind a guard that keeps writes on localhost and refuses browser profiles and saved routines. Off: only your capabilities.json reaches workers.

verifier.title: Independent verifier
verifier.description: A change that passes is checked again, before it counts, by a separate read-only worker that verifies the request, not the work, when its risk is high (data, security, money, a consumed contract, concurrency, delivery, or code changed with no test beside it) or medium and made by a cheap cell. Its findings go to the next attempt, two corrections at most. Off: a pass stands on its own check.

race.title: Race the next rung on a hard start
race.description: Where a kind's start rarely passes its first try in this repository (under half, over at least four), its first try runs beside the next rung, each in its own worktree; the first to pass its check is kept and the other stopped. It costs a second worker and saves the climb's wait. Off: one try at a time.

route.title: Choose the way for each request
route.description: Each request is read, with no model, for the way it is best done: by the session itself (small, reading, or about this conversation), by one worker that runs while the session goes on, or in parts side by side (large, or several areas). The session is told only when it is not itself, and decides. Off: the session chooses alone.

lean.title: Lean workers
lean.description: A worker gets no subagent tool (its description lists every agent the repository and you define, read on every turn), no skill listing (its role's skills are already in its brief), and its per-machine prompt sections after the part workers share, so the prompt cache serves more of it. Only flags your Claude Code supports are passed. Off: workers load what a session loads.

primer.title: Brief each worker with how its cell got oriented
primer.description: A passing worker says what it had to find before its first change; the next worker of its role or area starts from those lines. Each repository alternates tasks with and without them until each side has 12, then keeps the primer only where it won (fewer calls before the first change, first tries no worse). Off: no primer.

trunk.title: Workflow steps fork the step that read for them
trunk.description: A workflow step that names a reading step before it as its trunk (a plan, an exploration) starts as a fork of that step's session instead of reading the code again: its role reaches it as its first message after the fork, and the trunk's part is served by the prompt cache to every step that forks it. Each repository alternates forked and fresh first tries until each side has 10, then keeps forking only where it won (first tries no worse, fewer calls before the first change or less time). Off: every step starts fresh.

overlap.title: Run the independent check beside cauce's check
overlap.description: When a writing attempt passes and its change needs the independent verifier, the verifier starts at once, beside cauce's own check of the work, instead of after it: both read the same change, the verifier is told the check is running and not to run it itself, and a check that fails stops it (its cost is kept). Never for a task that starts services. Off: the verifier waits for the check.

role_trials.title: Improve each role's lessons by trial
role_trials.description: Once a role's workers met enough dead ends and verifier blockers in a repository, Haiku proposes a short list of lessons for that role there (the role's file is never touched). The role's tasks alternate with and without it until each side has 10 first tries; it is kept only where it passed first no worse and did better on one measure, and reverted if it later makes pass-first worse. `cauce roles revisions` shows them. Off: the role's own text alone.

habit_review.title: Review new habits with a worker
habit_review.description: A habit cauce newly finds in a project (an edit followed by the same check, again and again) is reviewed by a read-only worker: whether the tool is here, a command scoped to the edited file, run and timed. Its ending gives the install line, which the session puts to you; nothing is installed without your yes. Off: habits wait for `cauce habits`.

habit_auto.title: Install reviewed habits on their own
habit_auto.description: A habit the review worker proposes is installed by cauce once its own check passes: one simple command that runs the habit's program, passes on clean code at HEAD in a temporary worktree, finishes within 30 s and writes nothing. The ending says what was installed and the line that removes it; a habit that fails three times in a row, or keeps running past 60 s, turns itself off. Off: the session asks you before each install.

engram.title: Read the team's engram memory
engram.description: When an engram server runs (its session hook starts one, or `engram serve`), cauce searches the task's words in the project engram resolves for the checkout and puts the hits in the brief, and hands workers engram's MCP server read-only: saves, updates and deletes are refused by a guard, and every call stays in this project. cauce never opens engram's database itself. Off: engram is left alone.

engram_write.title: Save what workers learned in engram
engram_write.description: What a passing worker learned (the facts cauce keeps in its own notes: never a secret, never a failed attempt's, never text marked <private>) is also saved in engram as learning observations of the project, one session per task, so your team's agents find it. Off by default: it writes to a store that is not cauce's.

compact.title: Compact at the right moment
compact.description: cauce decides when a session should compact (a large context, at a break between tasks, while the prompt cache is warm, never while this session's run holds the checkout) and what /compact should keep, read from your requests verbatim and the session's open work. orchestrator: the orchestrating session is told at that moment and decides itself, compacting with the cauce compact tool (on that advice or on its own), with what it asks to keep. suggest: the mod shows you the /compact line to paste. auto: the mod has Claude Code compact with those instructions between turns; a build never seen to run it falls back to suggest and says so once. off: Claude Code's own auto-compaction alone.

delegate.title: Let the session start cauce work without asking
delegate.description: With Claude Code's mods: when Claude Code would ask you before the session queues or resumes a cauce task, the mod lets it through, so the orchestrator hands out work without waiting on you. A rule or a setting that denies it still denies it, an organization's limits still hold, and a resume the session starts still refuses what only you may clear (a Fable approval, a permission rule, keeping one). Off: you approve each queue and resume.

max_parallel.title: Workers at once
max_parallel.description: The most workers this machine runs at once, every repository's together. auto: no ceiling; cauce starts at what the machine can hold (its CPUs, free memory and free disk), adds one when work waits and the last tasks ended with no limit, and halves on a rate limit, an overloaded API, a worker the machine starved, or low memory or disk. A number: your ceiling, and the level still adapts under it. Each repository with work is reserved its share, and lends what it does not use. Cost never moves it.
